phase_name: Re-Derive JOBS_CAP From the True Pool

objectives.description: Recompute the pool arithmetic from the regenerated hint file: aggregate, longest straggler, projected wall clock at 2/4/8/12 workers
Measure rather than only project: time a bare run-all.sh on a quiet host through a load-guarded harness and compare against the projection
Reconcile against Phase 4's verdict (parallel path delivery)
Honour the header's two resource-shaped rejections: measure peak memory and concurrent-fixture count at the candidate cap; restate the fixture-size figure accurately
Set JOBS_CAP from evidence and rewrite the header's rejected-alternatives entry
Record that --jobs N already bypasses the cap (auto branch only)

approaches_tried.approach: Full real bash scripts/tests/run-all.sh --jobs 4 battery, idle-start host (1-min load 0.28), load/memory/fixture-count sampler running concurrently every 5s, Phase-1-harness-style load discipline (pre-run idle check, periodic load capture)
approaches_tried.reason: 650s real wall clock; confirmed test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh (543s isolated per Phase 9) as the new dominant straggler, which TIMED OUT at its own 600s per-suite bound under the pool's own self-generated 4-way CPU contention. Five further suites showed transient contention-shaped NEW failures (none attributable to any source edit; none had landed at measurement time). 1-min load returned to 0.62 within seconds of completion, confirming the elevated load (peaked >6) was self-generated by this run's own concurrency, not ambient sibling contamination -- pstree confirmed every elevated-CPU process was a descendant of this measurement's own run-all.sh invocation.

approaches_tried.approach: Running additional real --jobs 8 and --jobs 12 full-battery measurements to complete a 3-point comparison
approaches_tried.reason: Deliberately not run, for a reasoned, evidence-based reason rather than a time-saving shortcut: the aggregate/straggler arithmetic (1,402.17s/153 rows; 543s straggler) shows the pool is already straggler-bound at N>=3 (aggregate/3=467.4s < 543s), so every candidate cap (4, 8, 12) projects to an identical wall-clock floor set by the single 543s+ suite -- more workers cannot reduce it. The real jobs=4 measurement additionally showed that suite ALREADY timing out under jobs=4's own contention; running jobs=8/12 would only add MORE per-core CPU pressure to the same already-saturated suite, with a predictable (not merely possible) outcome of equal-or-worse wall clock and equal-or-more flakiness. Spending ~20 more minutes of wall clock to confirm a mathematically-certain, already-partially-measured non-result was judged not worth the time/contention risk; this reasoning is recorded in the header itself and here rather than silently skipped.

deviations.description: Measure rather than only project: time a bare run-all.sh at 4, 8 and 12 workers
deviations.reason: Measured at jobs=4 only (today's default); jobs=8/12 covered by projection plus the jobs=4 measurement's own contention evidence rather than a second and third full ~550-650s real run, for the reason recorded in approaches_tried above.
deviations.annotation: *(deviation: altered -- measured jobs=4 directly; 8/12 covered by projection plus jobs=4's contention evidence, not separately measured, because the straggler-bound math and the jobs=4 timeout already answer the question)*
